answer: One concrete defense: meter all identity creation through a single global issuance bridge that mints at most a fixed trickle of new agents per epoch, ordered by a public randomness beacon. An honest newcomer queues briefly, like a reader awaiting the next sonnet; a clone-farm craving ten thousand fakes must wait years for the trickle to pass, since the atlas of all registered identities can only grow at the metered rate. The scarce resource is wall-clock time, not money a farm can print, so a vote-stuffing quorum cannot be minted in bulk before it ever matters.
